issue.body_normalized: When using the Jupyter notebook workspaces in PrairieLearn, my students and I are frequently getting the error "XSRF Cookies do not match Post Argument", which (depending on when it occurs) prevents users from either launching kernels or saving files. Unfortunately, at the moment I don't have many useful details to add. - It happens on all browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) - I don't see any pattern to when it happens. The problem usually happens when opening the notebook; but, sometimes it pops up after having been working in the notebook for awhile. - Refreshing the page and/or opening/closing the notebook doesn't usually fix the problem. - Sometimes opening the workbook in a new browser works, sometimes it doesn't. - Eventually the problem just goes away. For example, it's not uncommon for the error to simply go away if I walk away for 5 minutes or so. The PrairieLearn people have looked and, from what they can tell, the issue seems to be entirely in jupyter. ## Reproduce The bug is intermittent. It appears seemingly at random when opening a workbook. ## Expected behavior No XSRF errors. ## Context - Operating System and version: All. (I use macOS 13.5) - Browser and version: All. (I use Chrome 116.0.5845.110) - JupyterLab version: 2.2.9 Here is one example of some workbooks that exhibited the error. I'm not sure how to get you all access; but, I can ask the PrairieLearn people when you get a chance to dig in: https://us.prairielearn.com/pl/workspace/1105215 https://us.prairielearn.com/pl/workspace/1112412 https://us.prairielearn.com/pl/workspace/1112414 https://us.prairielearn.com/pl/workspace/1105701 I'll try to add details as I think of what to capture. (The challenge is that this tends to happen during class, so I usually can't stop and dig into the developer console.)
